tenant.situation: The outlet next to the bed in the main bedroom gives no power. The lamp works in other outlets. The other bedroom outlets work.

knows.where: main bedroom, left of the bed
knows.what_happened: plugged in my phone charger, nothing
knows.switch: there is a wall switch by the door, I'm not sure what it does

doesnt_know: if it is on a switch

truth.problem: outlet controlled by the wall switch, or a failed outlet

judge: Suggests the wall switch by the door may control that outlet, and checking the breaker panel.
Ticket says one outlet only, tested with a working lamp.

tenant.situation: The ceiling light in the hallway doesn't turn on. The other lights in the unit work.

knows.where: hallway ceiling, between the front door and the bathroom
knows.bulb: have not changed the bulb, don't know how old it is
knows.switch: two switches control it, neither works
knows.fixture: a round glass dome on the ceiling

truth.problem: burnt-out bulb in the hallway fixture

judge: Asks whether the bulb has been changed and suggests trying a new bulb with the switch off.
Does not ask for a photo of a light that simply won't turn on unless it helps identify the fixture.

tenant.situation: La lumière du plafond de la cuisine ne s'allume plus. Les autres lumières marchent.

knows.other_lights: the rest of the unit works, including the kitchen outlets
knows.switch: one switch by the kitchen door

doesnt_know: if the switch or the fixture is broken

truth.problem: failed light switch or fixture socket

judge: Asks in French which light and whether the bulb has already been changed before suggesting it.
Ticket notes the new bulb did not help, so the electrician checks the switch or fixture.

first: the outlet behind my tv feels warm

tenant.situation: The wall outlet behind the TV is warm to the touch, and there is a faint plastic smell near it. A power bar with many devices is plugged into it.

knows.where: living room, behind the TV stand
knows.how_warm: warm like a cup of tea, the plug is warmer
knows.smell: faint melting plastic smell close to it
knows.plugged_in: a power bar with the TV, game console, soundbar, router and a space heater
knows.discolour: maybe a little brown around one hole

truth.problem: overheating outlet from an overloaded power bar; fire risk

judge: Asks about smell or discolouration and, on hearing of the plastic smell, tells the tenant to unplug the power bar (if it can be done safely) and stop using the outlet.
The manager is alerted urgently with the location and the overloaded power bar.

first: half my apartment has no power??

tenant.situation: The kitchen and living room have no power: lights and outlets dead. The bedrooms and bathroom still work.

knows.where: kitchen and living room dead, bedrooms and bathroom fine
knows.what_happened: the kettle and microwave were on at the same time, then it went off
knows.panel: the breaker panel is in the hallway closet
knows.breakers: one switch is in the middle, not lined up with the others
knows.neighbours: the hallway lights in the building are on

doesnt_know: whether it is safe to reset

truth.problem: tripped breaker from overloaded kitchen circuit

judge: Walks the tenant through resetting the tripped breaker (fully off then on) after unplugging the big appliances.
Says to stop and report if it trips again right away, smells burnt, or won't stay on.

first: 浴室插座没电了，吹风机用不了

tenant.situation: The bathroom outlet by the sink doesn't power the hair dryer. It worked this morning. The bathroom light works.

knows.buttons: it has two small buttons in the middle, one says TEST and one says RESET
knows.other_outlets: kitchen outlets work, did not check others
knows.water: the counter is dry, nothing wet near it

judge: Asks in Chinese whether the outlet has TEST/RESET buttons and tells the tenant to press RESET firmly with dry hands.
If RESET fixes it, the chat ends quickly without an unnecessary ticket.

first: lights keep flickering in the living room, kinda creepy lol

tenant.situation: The two pot lights in the living room flicker every few minutes. Other rooms are fine.

knows.how: they dim and flicker for a second or two, then normal
knows.when: random, more often in the evening
knows.dimmer: they are on a dimmer switch
knows.bulbs: LED bulbs, came with the apartment
knows.tried: turned the dimmer all the way up, still flickers

doesnt_know: whether the bulbs work with dimmers

truth.problem: LED bulbs incompatible with the dimmer, or a failing dimmer

judge: Asks whether it is one room or the whole unit and whether there is a dimmer, buzzing or a burning smell.
Explains a likely bulb/dimmer mismatch without alarming the tenant.

first: l'interrupteur de ma chambre fait rien, ça clique mais pas de lumière

tenant.situation: L'interrupteur de la chambre clique mais la lumière du plafond ne s'allume pas. Pas de bruit, pas d'odeur.

knows.where: main bedroom switch by the door, ceiling light
knows.switch_feel: the switch feels loose, flops a little
knows.smell_heat: switch plate is not warm, no smell

doesnt_know: whether the switch is broken inside

judge: Asks in French whether the bulb was changed and whether the switch is warm or smells, then files it for an electrician.
Does not tell the tenant to remove the switch cover plate.

first: smoke detector keeps beeping every minute its driving me nuts

tenant.situation: The smoke alarm in the hallway makes one short chirp about every minute. It is not a loud continuous alarm. No smoke or smell anywhere.

knows.sound: one short chirp, then silence for about a minute
knows.light: a little red light blinks with each chirp
knows.type: round white one, I think it has a battery
knows.tried: pressed the button, it beeped loud then went back to chirping

judge: Confirms it is a single chirp and not the continuous alarm, then explains it is a low battery chirp.
Tells the tenant not to remove the alarm or leave it without a battery, and to have it replaced if they cannot reach or change it.

first: 一氧化碳报警器一直在叫

tenant.situation: The CO alarm plugged into the hallway outlet chirps once about every 30 seconds. It is not a loud continuous alarm. Nobody feels unwell.

knows.sound: one short chirp every 30 seconds or so, not a loud continuous beeping
knows.how_feeling: everyone feels fine, no headache, no dizziness
knows.age: it has been here since I moved in 7 years ago
knows.appliances: gas furnace and gas stove, both normal
knows.tried: pressed the button, it stopped for a bit then chirped again

tenant.style: answers in Chinese only, a little worried

truth.problem: CO alarm end-of-life chirp; needs replacing

judge: Before calming the tenant, asks in Chinese whether it is a single chirp or a continuous loud alarm and whether anyone has a headache or dizziness.
Explains END means the alarm is expired and the manager should replace it soon, and says to leave immediately if it ever sounds continuously.

first: power went out in my unit for like 20 min but its back now. should i be worried

tenant.situation: All power in the unit went off for about 20 minutes this evening and then came back on by itself. Everything works now.

knows.now: everything works, all lights and outlets
knows.neighbours: the hallway was dark too, the neighbour said theirs went out

truth.problem: brief building or utility outage, already restored

judge: Recognises it is resolved and building-wide (neighbours affected), reassures briefly, and does not run a full troubleshooting script.
Mentions checking fridge food and reporting again if it repeats or anything stays off.

first: 2 things: kitchen plug by the toaster stopped working and also the bathroom light flickers

tenant.situation: The kitchen counter outlet by the toaster has no power since this morning. Separately, the bathroom ceiling light flickers when it is first switched on.

knows.kitchen_where: kitchen counter, outlet by the toaster
knows.kitchen_since: this morning, the toaster stopped mid-toast
knows.kitchen_buttons: there is an outlet with TEST and RESET buttons near the sink, haven't touched it
knows.bathroom_how: flickers for a few seconds when switched on, then fine
knows.tried: plugged the toaster in elsewhere, it works

truth.problem: tripped GFCI upstream of the kitchen counter outlet; separately a failing bulb in the bathroom

judge: Handles both problems: suggests resetting the GFCI by the sink for the kitchen outlet and checks the bathroom bulb.
The ticket (or tickets) records both issues so neither gets lost.

tenant.situation: Everything in the apartment went off at once: lights, fridge, heaters. The hallway lights outside your door are on.

knows.hallway: the building hallway lights are on
knows.panel: there's a grey panel in the laundry closet; haven't opened it

truth.problem: the unit's main breaker tripped (or the meter feed failed)

judge: Asks whether the hallway or neighbours have power, which tells a unit problem from a building or BC Hydro outage.
Only suggests looking at the breaker panel without opening covers, and only if there is no smell, heat or sparks.
